name: TA-10-anisotropic-grid
why: cellMetresX (3 m) and cellMetresY (1 m) differ, as a geographic grid at high latitude would (unequal east/west vs. north/south metres per cell, e.g. cos(60°N)). The plane tilts along the physically-longer X axis (tangent 1 in physical metres east), so an isotropic (bug) implementation that mistook a raster diagonal offset for a 45° physical heading, or ignored cellMetresX in the gradient scale, would compute a different longitudinal/cross-slope split and a different route cost than one that scales correctly. Both implementations share one raster-to-metres convention, and this pins that they agree on it.
